text:
SUPERSEDES the margin-threshold note below. That note is still TRUE and still load-bearing - margin >= 0.05 remains at lineage.py:258, and below it clone-heavy repos poison metadata migration. It went stale only because 0.54.0 changed this function's behaviour around it, so restating it here re-stamps it against the current logic.

New in 0.54.0, and the reason the body moved: detect_lineage takes use_sketch. When the sketches on disk came from a different shingle hash than this build's (Indexer.stale_sketches), the minhash signal cannot be compared at all, and the response is to EXCLUDE it rather than score it 0.0 - score_pair renormalizes over the remaining weights so 0.33 and 0.55 keep meaning what they meant. Scoring an unmeasured signal as zero would scale every score by 0.70 and silently move every threshold.

Two further consequences in that mode: split/merge detection is skipped wholesale, because sketch_containment has no fallback signal and running it would fabricate rather than weaken an answer; and terminal deletions are recorded with author="pending-review" and an explanatory note instead of "auto", because "true deletion" is a claim this index has not earned. Verified on the real migration of this repo: detect_lineage._r became an alias for the extracted _ratio and was filed pending-review with the reason attached, where before it would have read `deleted, author=auto`.

The scoring weights now live at module level (_SIGNAL_WEIGHTS) specifically so a test can reach them - as a closure the renormalization could not be falsified.
